cell_edits.Registration fee (USD): low (~US$65: MEC inscription fee UYU 2,530, subject to update; plus DGR registry fee)

finding: The official gub.uy procedure page shows MEC recognition of asociaciones civiles and fundaciones carries a tasa de inscripción of UYU 2,530 (about US$63), above the US$10-30 previously stated. Recognition is granted by the Ministerio de Educación y Cultura via its Oficina de Asuntos Constitucionales y Legales; foundations must prove initial capital. No official processing time is published.

cell_edits.Main charitable entity types: Private foundation (хувийн сан); Association (нийгмийн эвлэл); NGO under the Law on Non-Governmental Organizations (1997, foundations chapter 2002) + Civil Code (2002)
cell_edits.Key local requirements: As a Mongolian citizen (or legally resident foreigner) you register with the General Authority for State Registration with a Mongolian-language notarized charter, a local registered address, and a governing board (minimum 5 members for non-membership NGOs); a foundation requires an endowment adequate to its stated purpose; foreign NGO branches register with the Immigration Agency.

finding: ICNL's Civic Freedom Monitor (updated 15 May 2026) shows the governing statute is the 1997 Law on Non-Governmental Organizations, not a 'Law on Associations'; draft Laws on Associations/Foundations and a draft Law on Not-for-profit Legal Entities remain unadopted. Domestic NGOs register with the General Authority for State Registration and foreign NGO branches with the Immigration Agency. Foreigners legally residing in Mongolia may establish NGOs.

cell_edits.Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Local office, endowment set by each competent authority (e.g. Taipei NT$10m cash), Chinese-language docs, court registration and local counsel

finding: Taipei City rules set a NT$10 million cash minimum for social welfare foundations, and MOFA guidance shows thresholds vary by competent authority (e.g. NT$15m for recognised foreign international-cooperation foundations), so the fixed NT$15m local / NT$30m central tiers in the bottleneck cell are not a uniform rule. Foundations need competent-authority approval (decision within 60 days, extendable) followed by district court registration.

The Macau government portal confirms the procedure: DSI name-availability certificate, notarised constitution at a public notary, publication in the Boletim Oficial, then DSI registration number issued. A draft 'Legal Regime of Associations' making the DSI the unified oversight authority has been in public consultation and is not yet enacted. No official fee schedule was found to refine the cost estimate.

Law-firm sources confirm foundations are registered under the Civil and Commercial Code with the Ministry of Interior registrar (district office in Bangkok, Provincial Governor elsewhere), with THB 500,000 assets (or 250,000 for public-charity objects) and vetting/interview of foreign directors. Sources disagree on whether a Thai-majority board is required, consistent with the cell's 'practice, not statute' framing; the THB 210 fee was not independently re-confirmed.

cell_edits.Main charitable entity types: Association under Decree on Associations No. 536 (2025, replacing Decree 238/GOV of 2017); foundation under the foundations decree; INGO under Decree No. 126/GOV of 25 May 2026 (in force 15 Jul 2026, replacing PM Decree 013/2010)

finding: CIVICUS Monitor (June 2026), citing the UN Special Rapporteur's February 2026 report, states that Decree No. 536 (2025) on associations replaced Decree No. 238 (2017). Rajah & Tann and VDB Loi confirm INGO Decree No. 126/GOV of 25 May 2026, gazetted 11 June 2026 and effective 15 July 2026, replaced the 2010 INGO decree and requires prior MOFA approval before assisting local associations/foundations.

DFDL and Allen & Gledhill confirm the SAC's Organization Registration Law (Notification 46/2022, 28 Oct 2022) repealed the 2014 Association Registration Law, with MOHA issuing certificates after review by the Union/Region/State Registration Boards. INGOs must have at least 40% Myanmar citizens on the executive committee and file audited annual reports.

The Royal Brunei Police Force site confirms societies register under the Societies Act (Chapter 203) with the Registrar of Societies, a unit of the police Criminal Intelligence Department at Police HQ Gadong, contactable in person or by email. No official fee schedule is published online, so the BND 20 figure could not be confirmed.

Decree-Law No. 5/2005 on non-profit corporate bodies remains the governing instrument, with no repeal found; an EU Country Focus Report (Oct 2025) still cites it alongside the Civil Code (Law 10/2011). It provides for associations and foundations and for registration of foreign corporate bodies with a permanent local representative; registration runs through the Ministry of Justice's national registration directorate.

cell_edits.Est. cost & time: Incorporation fees in the low hundreds of USD (in PNGK); a few weeks for companies; new associations regime in force since 1 July 2026 adds a 60-day public objection period; foreign participation restricted in practice.
cell_edits.Key local requirements: Company: resident company secretary in PNG and local registered office. Association (2023 Act): committee of 3+ and public officer, each with at least one PNG-ordinarily-resident person; PNG registered office; newspaper notice of intent.

finding: IPA guidance confirms the Associations Incorporation Act 2023 commenced 1 July 2026, with free re-registration of existing associations due by 30 June 2027. New associations file a Notice of Intent, publish it in a national newspaper (60-day objection window), and need a committee of at least 3 and a public officer, each including at least one person ordinarily resident in PNG, plus a PNG registered office. Fees for new incorporation are not published on the page.

The Samoa Business Registries fee schedule confirms a $250 (WST) fee to register a company under s.6 of the Companies Act 2001. The registry's director guidance lists qualifications (natural person, 21+, not bankrupt, physical and postal address) but states no Samoa-residency requirement, and the Act text on PacLII could not be retrieved, so the 'resident director' claim could not be confirmed or refuted.

cell_edits.Key local requirements: Resident service agent and local registered office for companies (2014 Regs); charitable trusts incorporate as a Board with the Registrar of Charitable Trusts (= Registrar of Incorporated Societies, MCCTIL); foreign investor certification if overseas shareholders

finding: The Charitable Trusts Act 1993 defines the Registrar as the Registrar of Incorporated Societies, administered by MCCTIL's Business Registries Office, not a Ministry of Justice trust registry; trustees apply on Form 1 signed by a majority to incorporate as a Board. The MCCTIL company how-to requires a Tongan registered office and Foreign Investor Certification where shareholders are overseas. No statutory trustee-residency requirement was found in the Act.
